scope.name: production-complete-v1
scope.claim: Covers every landform in ontology.v1 plus production mesh subtypes needed to keep named rocks recognizable. It is not a claim to enumerate every landform on Earth.
scope.canonicalBaselineRule: A seeded deformation is a variation, not a new baseline. Only a separately reviewed mesh with its own nature-reference comparison counts toward minimumCanonicalBaselines.
scope.variationRule: Variation may change proportions and local relief only inside the selected profile and identity metrics. It may not change topology, named landform, support logic, or defining silhouette.
scope.failureRule: Any forbidden drift or failed identity metric rejects the mesh even when topology, UV, bake, and runtime checks pass.

families.label: Detached clasts
families.definition: Individual transportable or fallen rock pieces classified separately by size, shape, fabric, and abrasion.

families.label: Residuals and outcrops
families.definition: Attached bedrock masses whose silhouette is controlled by joints, exfoliation, fabric, or differential weathering.

families.label: Fins, spires, and hoodoos
families.definition: Vertically dominant residuals with distinct width, taper, caprock, and structural-control rules.

families.label: Rock surfaces and steps
families.definition: Pavements, terraces, ledges, benches, and mounds defined by plan continuity and step geometry.

families.label: Cliffs and scarps
families.definition: Continuous terrain or modules with a readable face, crest, toe, structure, and termination.

families.label: Caves, arches, and bridges
families.definition: Host-rock masses with geologically supported cavities or through-openings.

families.label: Coastal residuals
families.definition: Wave-cut remnants representing a specific stage in cliff-cave-arch-stack-stump retreat.

families.label: Plateaus and badlands
families.definition: Layer-controlled erosional remnants and dissected terrain with recognizable summit and flank proportions.

families.label: Intrusions
families.definition: Dykes, sills, and veins represented with host contacts and correct sheet orientation.

families.label: Volcanic and cooling forms
families.definition: Necks, domes, and column systems controlled by emplacement, flow, and cooling surfaces.

families.label: Ridges and massifs
families.definition: Formation-scale silhouettes with coherent drainage, structure, peaks, saddles, and assembly modules.

families.label: Deposits and fields
families.definition: Multi-clast landforms whose identity comes from sorting, source direction, fabric, and gravity or flow organization.

subtypes.label: Splintery shard

subtypes.label: Glacial erratic

subtypes.label: Spheroidal corestone

unequal joint-controlled lobes
requiredStructure: rounding advances inward from joints and corners

subtypes.label: Massive outcrop
requiredSilhouette: attached bedrock exposure with continuous base

requiredStructure: massive fabric remains subordinate to finite joints

subtypes.label: Jointed outcrop

requiredStructure: finite joint sets control blocks and recesses

subtypes.label: Bedded outcrop

subtypes.label: Pillow-lava outcrop
requiredSilhouette: overlapping bulbous lobes with pinched contacts
broken faces expose pillow cross-sections
requiredStructure: lobes stack and drape with gravity and flow direction

subtypes.label: Block-pile tor
requiredSilhouette: recognizable pile of large joint-derived residual masses
irregular skyline with ledges and deep joints
broad bedrock-connected base
requiredStructure: blocks share joint ancestry and remain gravity-supported

subtypes.label: Castellated tor
requiredSilhouette: castle-like towers and notches formed by joint blocks
multiple unequal crowns on a continuous base
requiredStructure: orthogonal or suborthogonal joints create the castellated outline

subtypes.label: Freestanding tor
requiredSilhouette: isolated residual stack with two or more joint masses

requiredStructure: visible supported contacts and shared weathering history

subtypes.label: Massive monolith

vertically legible base, body, and crown
requiredStructure: joints subdivide surface without turning the mass into a stack

subtypes.label: Jointed monolith

requiredStructure: joint traces persist and terminate plausibly

subtypes.label: Exfoliation dome

steepening lower flanks and attached base
requiredStructure: sheet joints roughly follow surface curvature

subtypes.label: Sandstone fin
requiredSilhouette: long narrow wall of rock
continuous crest with local notches
requiredStructure: parallel joints or bedding isolate a slab-like ridge

subtypes.label: Rock blade

sharp or serrated crest
requiredStructure: resistant bed, dyke, or joint-bounded sheet controls the blade

subtypes.label: Rock spire or needle
requiredSilhouette: slender isolated vertically dominant residual

requiredStructure: joints, bedding, or resistant rock explain survival

subtypes.label: Volcanic spine

requiredStructure: flow banding or cooling joints align with emplacement

subtypes.label: Residual pinnacle
requiredSilhouette: isolated prominent peak or tower
irregular crown narrower than base
requiredStructure: resistant mass remains tied to coherent bedrock

subtypes.label: Residual pillar

requiredStructure: differential erosion or joint isolation controls shaft

subtypes.label: Singular karst spire

requiredStructure: joints, bedding, and dissolution jointly control ledges and runnels

subtypes.label: Tiered karst tower

narrower crown over a continuous buttressed base

subtypes.label: Caprock hoodoo
requiredSilhouette: resistant cap wider than an eroded neck or shaft
stable base and asymmetric cap
requiredStructure: cap and shaft correspond to contrasting resistance

subtypes.label: Tapered hoodoo
requiredSilhouette: tapered erosional column with irregular ledges and recesses
material-controlled profile
requiredStructure: differential erosion follows real bed resistance changes

subtypes.label: Jointed rock pavement

requiredStructure: joint polygons remain part of continuous bedrock

subtypes.label: Limestone pavement

subtypes.label: Massive rock mound
requiredSilhouette: low broad convex attached mass

requiredStructure: weathering follows lithology and joints

subtypes.label: Depositional rock mound
requiredSilhouette: lobate or terraced accretionary mound
irregular drapes and vents
requiredStructure: growth layers wrap the mound rather than cut horizontally through space

subtypes.label: Rock-cut terrace
requiredSilhouette: broad tread bounded by a riser
continuous connection to adjacent terrain
requiredStructure: erosion surface truncates underlying fabric where appropriate

subtypes.label: Travertine terrace
requiredSilhouette: nested or branching pool rims
draped terrace fronts
requiredStructure: precipitate growth follows water flow and spills

subtypes.label: Resistant rock ledge
requiredSilhouette: outward-projecting resistant band or slab
clear back contact and eroded recess below or above
requiredStructure: ledge follows a bed, sill, vein, or resistant domain

subtypes.label: Erosional bench
requiredSilhouette: broad near-level step cut into a larger slope or cliff
continuous rear wall or upslope connection
requiredStructure: bench elevation follows resistance or erosional process

subtypes.label: Broad rock wall
requiredSilhouette: continuous elongated face with readable crest and toe
terrain-connected ends or explicit module seams
requiredStructure: surface relief follows bedding, joints, or fabric

subtypes.label: Massive cliff
requiredSilhouette: steep continuous face
irregular crest, toe, buttresses, and recesses
requiredStructure: massive fabric with finite joint-controlled failures

subtypes.label: Jointed block cliff
requiredSilhouette: continuous face divided into interlocking blocks

requiredStructure: joint persistence and spacing vary within declared sets

subtypes.label: Bedded cliff

requiredStructure: bedding has coherent strike and dip with truncation and joint offsets

subtypes.label: Foliated cliff
requiredSilhouette: steep continuous face with fabric-guided ribs or slabs

requiredStructure: foliation folds, offsets, or wraps domains instead of forming sedimentary courses

subtypes.label: Columnar cliff
requiredSilhouette: continuous lava-flow cliff expressed as adjoining prisms

subtypes.label: Massive sea cliff
requiredSilhouette: steep coastal face with wave-cut toe
headland continuity and irregular crest
requiredStructure: jointing controls caves, notches, and failures

subtypes.label: Bedded sea cliff
requiredSilhouette: stepped coastal face with wave-cut toe
bed-controlled ledges and slump or rockfall scars
requiredStructure: bedding and joints continue through coastal openings

subtypes.label: Supported cliff overhang
requiredSilhouette: projecting roof attached to a larger mass
readable back wall, roof thickness, and load path
requiredStructure: undercut follows weaker bed, joint, cave, or erosion process

subtypes.label: Canyon wall
requiredSilhouette: long continuous valley-bounding wall
tributary gullies, buttresses, ledges, and talus toe
requiredStructure: paired regional structure and drainage explain the face

subtypes.label: Rock gorge
requiredSilhouette: narrow incision bounded by two related rock walls

requiredStructure: opposed walls share lithology and structural history

subtypes.label: Escarpment
requiredSilhouette: regional linear steep slope separating gentler surfaces
long crest with embayments and spurs
requiredStructure: erosion or structure explains consistent regional orientation

subtypes.label: Fault scarp
requiredSilhouette: linear terrain break with displaced surfaces

requiredStructure: scarp follows a fault trace and offsets markers

subtypes.label: Bedrock slope
requiredSilhouette: continuous inclined terrain surface
convex, straight, or concave profile tied to process
requiredStructure: outcrop bands, gullies, and debris follow slope and fabric

subtypes.label: Straight cliff module

requiredStructure: bedding or joints continue across seams without visible phase reset

subtypes.label: Cliff corner module
requiredSilhouette: terrain-connected wall turning through a readable corner

requiredStructure: fabric bends geometrically only when geology permits; otherwise it crosses the corner

subtypes.label: Cliff termination module
requiredSilhouette: wall face resolves into a spur, slope, buttress, or buried end

requiredStructure: beds, joints, and ledges terminate or wrap plausibly

subtypes.label: Karst cave mouth
requiredSilhouette: finite entrance cut into a continuous limestone host
readable roof, walls, floor, and receding darkness
requiredStructure: opening follows joints, bedding, and dissolution paths

subtypes.label: Volcanic cave mouth
requiredSilhouette: entrance within lava, welded tuff, or lodged talus host

requiredStructure: void follows lava tube, cooling fracture, or inter-block cavity

subtypes.label: Sea cave
requiredSilhouette: cavity opening at the foot of a sea cliff or headland
wave-cut floor and narrowing interior
requiredStructure: joint, fault, or weaker bed guides marine erosion

subtypes.label: Sandstone natural arch
requiredSilhouette: through-opening in a once-continuous fin or rock mass
two abutments and an intact load-bearing roof
requiredStructure: bedding and joints continue across the roof where preserved
forbiddenDrift: two pillars with a slab placed on top

subtypes.label: Sea arch
requiredSilhouette: through-opening in a coastal headland or sea cliff
wave-cut floor, abutments, and roof
requiredStructure: opening enlarges from joint-guided sea caves

subtypes.label: Natural bridge
requiredSilhouette: rock span over a former or active stream course
massive abutments and continuous roof
requiredStructure: channel incision and meander cutoff or cave collapse explain opening

subtypes.label: Sea stack
requiredSilhouette: steep isolated coastal pillar detached from a headland

requiredStructure: beds or joints correlate with the parent sea cliff

subtypes.label: Sea stump

subtypes.label: Mesa
requiredSilhouette: broad isolated flat-to-gently-dipping summit

requiredStructure: beds continue across summit and flank ledges

subtypes.label: Butte

requiredStructure: caprock and lower beds preserve regional stratigraphy

subtypes.label: Dissected badlands
requiredSilhouette: densely dissected ridges, gullies, walls, and residuals
nested drainage hierarchy and sparse cover
requiredStructure: erodibility contrasts in layered sediment control walls and hoodoos

subtypes.label: Dyke wall
requiredSilhouette: steep tabular rib or wall cross-cutting host terrain
finite tapered or buried ends
requiredStructure: contacts cross host bedding and may chill or fracture
forbiddenDrift: free rock fin with no host relationship

subtypes.label: Sill
requiredSilhouette: subhorizontal resistant sheet or ledge within host strata
contacts remain traceable
requiredStructure: sheet is broadly concordant with host layering

subtypes.label: Mineral vein rib
requiredSilhouette: thin cross-cutting mineralized sheet or resistant rib
branching or pinching finite trace
requiredStructure: vein occupies fractures and cuts or offsets host fabric

subtypes.label: Volcanic neck
requiredSilhouette: resistant central volcanic mass exposed above eroded host
steep irregular flanks and coherent crown
requiredStructure: cooling joints or intrusive contacts reflect plug geometry

subtypes.label: Blocky lava dome
requiredSilhouette: steep-sided lobate dome

requiredStructure: flow lobes and fractures follow extrusion direction

subtypes.label: Flow-banded lava dome

subtypes.label: Basalt colonnade

subtypes.label: Basalt entablature

subtypes.label: Tiered colonnade-entablature flow

subtypes.label: Radial or curved columns

requiredStructure: local column direction stays normal to the curved cooling surface

subtypes.label: Massive rock ridge

requiredStructure: jointing and erosion remain coherent along ridge length

subtypes.label: Stratified ridge

subtypes.label: Folded ridge

requiredStructure: beds remain ordered through limbs and hinges

subtypes.label: Shattered alpine ridge
requiredSilhouette: sharp serrated crest with peaks, notches, and descending ribs
fractured walls and talus aprons
requiredStructure: frost shattering and joints produce finite blocks

subtypes.label: Exfoliation massif

sheeted crowns over jointed lower walls
requiredStructure: exfoliation sheets follow topography and regional joints

subtypes.label: Volcanic massif

requiredStructure: flows, dykes, plugs, and drainage share volcanic center context

subtypes.label: Karst tower field

subtypes.label: Modular bedrock mountain
requiredSilhouette: coherent mountain with primary peaks, secondary buttresses, ledges, and tertiary fracture detail
continuous drainage and contact hierarchy across modules
requiredStructure: modules share formation-local bedding, joints, erosion, texel density, and connectors

subtypes.label: Boulder field
requiredSilhouette: terrain-spanning concentration of overlapping boulders
irregular exposed and buried fractions
requiredStructure: size, angularity, and orientation reflect source and process

subtypes.label: Talus fan

requiredStructure: clast lithology matches source and fabric follows gravity

subtypes.label: Scree sheet

requiredStructure: clast size and fabric grade downslope plausibly

subtypes.label: Rockfall deposit
requiredSilhouette: irregular angular debris accumulation below a fresh scar

requiredStructure: blocks correlate with missing source mass and joint sets

subtypes.label: Bouldery moraine
requiredSilhouette: ridge, hummock, or sheet of poorly sorted glacial debris
embedded erratics of mixed sizes
requiredStructure: fabric and landform align with ice margin or flow direction

subtypes.label: River gravel bar
requiredSilhouette: low elongate or lobate deposit within a channel
partially buried sorted pebbles, cobbles, and boulders
requiredStructure: imbrication, sorting, and bar shape align with flow
forbiddenDrift: dry mound with no channel context

subtypes.label: Beach ridge
requiredSilhouette: low shore-parallel ridge or berm of sorted clasts
seaward and landward slopes remain distinct
requiredStructure: clast sorting, rounding, and imbrication reflect wave action
